title: Banksy's self-shredding painting
hook: A Banksy painting shredded itself seconds after selling for over a million pounds.
peek: In 2018, moments after Banksy's Girl with Balloon sold at Sotheby's in London, a shredder hidden in its frame pulled the canvas halfway through. The half-shredded work was renamed and later sold again for many times the price.
lede: On 5 October 2018, a framed Banksy painting of Girl with Balloon sold at Sotheby's in London for just over £1 million including fees. As the hammer fell, an alarm sounded and the canvas began sliding down through the bottom of the ornate gilt frame, coming out in strips. A shredder had been hidden inside the frame, and it stopped about halfway.

bullets.text: The image began as a stencil Banksy painted on a wall in London's South Bank in 2002: a small girl reaching for a red, heart-shaped balloon drifting away from her. It became one of his best-known pictures.
Banksy later posted a video showing the mechanism being built into the frame years earlier. He said it was meant to shred the whole canvas, and that it had worked every time in rehearsals.

bullets.opening: Renamed Love is in the Bin
bullets.text: The buyer, a European collector, decided to keep the work. Banksy's authentication office gave it a new title, Love is in the Bin, treating the shredding as part of a new artwork.
Three years later, the half-shredded canvas came back to Sotheby's and sold for about £18.6 million, roughly eighteen times its 2018 price and a record for Banksy at auction at the time.
